blocks.text: Verses 31–34 name a “new covenant,” a renewed relationship promised to both the houses of Israel and Judah. Its features are God’s instruction, or Torah, written in people’s inward parts and hearts; shared knowledge of YHWH from least to greatest; and forgiveness. Within a chapter filled with return, rebuilding, planting, mourning, and comfort, these promises present restoration without pretending that the earlier loss has not occurred.

Jeremiah 30–33 forms a restoration collection within the received book of Jeremiah. The book as a whole brings together varied forms, including poetry, prose sermons, narratives, letters, headings, repeated accounts, oracles concerning nations, and an appendix; its long compositional and textual history remains a matter of scholarly discussion. This broader setting helps locate Jeremiah 31’s restoration language within a larger collection rather than treating it as an isolated passage.
